rules.statement: A party's silence and continued acceptance of payments after knowledge of a sublet arrangement constitutes acknowledgment of the sublet.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) The plaintiff-respondent on her own admission knew for certain in 1981, that premises had been sublet to the 2nd defendant-appellant, she made no protest of any kind and continued to accept rent from the 2nd defendant-appellant. (2) It was open to the plaintiff-respondent to terminate the tenancy which was not availed of. (3) Condonation or waiver would operate as a bar to the exercise of the landlords statutory rights to secure the ejectment of the tenant on the ground of subletting. 254 (4) There was privity of contract established between the plaintiff-respondent and the 2nd defendant-appellant. (5) There is overwhelming evidence of waiver of the statutory right of the plaintiff-respondent to have the 1st defendant-respondent and 2nd defendant-appellant evicted
